detail.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The `muse`, `minicpm5` and `poolside_v1` tool parsers keep a parameter's raw text only when its schema is exactly `{"type": "string"}`, so `Optional[str]` values such as `"1.10"` or `"1984"` come back as `1.1` or `1984`. This makes them keep the raw text whenever the schema allows a string. The Rust frontend's Muse parser gets the same fix.

FIX #64517

## Claims

- String parameters keep their raw text when the schema allows a string through `anyOf`/`oneOf`, a `type` list, `enum`/`const`, a local `$ref`, `allOf`, or `additionalProperties`. Streaming and non-streaming both get the fix.
- Values that fit another type the schema allows still decode to it: `null` -> `None` for `Optional[str]`, `"25"` -> `25` under `anyOf [integer, string]`.
- Unchanged: plain `type: string`, non-string types, untyped parameters (`{}`), Python `muse_glimmer`, and `extract_types_from_schema` / `ParserEngine` coercion.

## Validation

| Check | main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| `pytest tests/tool_use/test_muse.py tests/tool_parsers/test_{schema_types,minicpm5xml_tool_parser,poolside_v1_tool_parser}.py` | `test_muse.py` and `test_schema_types.py` do not import (no `schema_types`); MiniCPM5 4 failed, 38 passed; Poolside 2 failed, 16 passed | 199 passed |
| `pytest tests/tool_parsers`, `pytest tests/parser` (without cohere), `pytest tests/tool_use/test_muse_glimmer.py` | 1227, 6783, 25 passed | 1264, 6783, 25 passed |
| `cargo test -p vllm-parser --locked` (Rust 1.95), `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p vllm-parser --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings` | | 625 passed (30 Muse, 29 on main), clean |
| B200, nightly image, served MiniCPM5-2B, Laguna-XS.2 and Muse-Glimmer-30B (`muse`): 12 string forms, 3 streaming and 3 non-streaming requests each | 6/6 wrong per form | 0/6 per form |
| Muse-Glimmer-30B on the Rust frontend (`vllm-rs`, `muse`): the same 12 forms | 6/6 wrong per form | 0/6 per form |
| 8x B200, Muse-Spark-816B (NVFP4, TP8), Python and Rust frontends: the same 12 forms ¹ | 6/6 wrong per form on both | 0/6 per form on both |
| Same servers: plain `string`, `null` on `Optional[str]`, `"25"` under `anyOf [integer, string]` | correct | correct |
| `muse_glimmer`, and `qwen3_coder` (ParserEngine) on Qwen3.5-0.8B | | identical to main |

¹ Spark ran on an earlier revision of this branch with the same rules. The final code was rerun on MiniCPM5, Laguna, Glimmer (Python and Rust) and Qwen3.5, and returned the same arguments as that revision on every request.

On Glimmer and on Spark, the Rust and Python frontends return identical arguments for every request, on main and on this PR.

The 12 forms are `anyOf [string, null]` (1984, true, a JSON body), `oneOf`, `["string", "null"]`, an untyped `enum`, `const`, a local `$ref`, `allOf [$ref, {description}]`, `additionalProperties`, `anyOf [integer, string]` with 1.10, and `["number", "string"]` with true.

`tests/tool_parsers/test_schema_types.py` table-tests every schema form once against `parameter_types` and `convert_value`. Each parser has a smoke test of `Optional[str]` through `extract_tool_calls` and `extract_tool_calls_streaming` with a real request (Muse: Chat and Responses).

Each parser builds its parameter types once, on first use, because the renderer builds a throwaway parser per request for `adjust_request`. Served streaming ITL on Muse-Glimmer with 40 tools x 20 parameters is within 0.3% of main (20.21 ms vs 20.19 ms, measured on the previous revision of this branch, which caches the same way).

Size against main (Rust inline tests counted as tests):

| | Code +/- | Tests +/- |
|---|---|---|
| Python | 203 / 116 | 132 / 7 |
| Rust | 63 / 24 | 57 / 4 |
| Total | 266 / 140 | 189 / 11 |

## Details

**Root cause.** Each parser compared the schema to `"type": "string"` (Muse `_string_parameters`, MiniCPM5 `_get_argument_type`, Poolside `_is_string_type`, Rust `MuseUnifiedParser::new`) and decoded everything else.

**Change.** `parameter_types` in the new `vllm/tool_parsers/schema_types.py` computes the JSON types each top-level parameter allows (`type`, `const`, `enum`, local `$ref`, `anyOf`/`oneOf` as union, `allOf` as intersection). `convert_value` keeps the raw text unless the parser's own decoder returns another allowed type. Each parser keeps its decoder. In Rust, Muse derives the types from the existing `SchemaRoot::options` walk, which already resolves `$ref` for coercion and the output grammars, and intersects multi-branch `allOf`, where a `number` branch also admits integers.

**Scope.** `extract_types_from_schema` and `ParserEngine` coercion are not touched; consolidating them is #63385. Structured-output schema analysis (RFC #58697) checks grammar-backend features, not value types.

**Limitations.**
- Only top-level parameters are checked; nested values are decoded as a whole.
- A union with an untyped branch (`anyOf [string, {}]`) is unconstrained, so it decodes, as on main.
- `anyOf [string, object]` decodes a JSON body to an object; the schema allows both.
- Poolside V1 streams `Optional[str]` arguments in one delta at `</arg_value>`, as on main.
- The Rust frontend uses one parser for Spark and Glimmer, so Rust Glimmer gets the new rules while Python Glimmer always decodes. This split predates this PR.

**Rust differs from Python** on a few schemas that admit a string:
- `allOf` nested inside `anyOf`;
- an untyped `anyOf` beside a `type` list;
- `$ref` chains deeper than 32, which decode as on main;
- the OpenAPI `nullable` null option.

The decoders also differ. serde_json rejects `NaN`/`Infinity` and reads integers beyond 64 bits as floats, so Rust keeps the raw text in cases where Python's `json.loads` decodes.

---

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+import json
+
+import pytest
+
+from vllm.tool_parsers.schema_types import convert_value, parameter_types
+
+_NULLABLE_STR = {"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}]}
+_INT_OR_STR = {"anyOf": [{"type": "integer"}, {"type": "string"}]}
+_BODY = '{\n  "version": "1.4.0",\n  "build": 7\n}'
+_DEFS = {
+    "S": {"type": "string"},
+    "C": {"allOf": [{"$ref": "#/$defs/C"}, {"type": "string"}]},
+    # Each def references the next one twice: 2**60 paths without memoization.
+    **{f"D{i}": {"anyOf": [{"$ref": f"#/$defs/D{i + 1}"}] * 2} for i in range(60)},
+    "D60": {"type": "string"},
+}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("schema", "raw", "expected"),
+    [
+        # plain string and non-string types: unchanged
+        ({"type": "string"}, "1.10", "1.10"),
+        ({"type": "integer"}, "1.10", 1.1),
+        # schemas that admit a string keep the raw text...
+        (_NULLABLE_STR, "1.10", "1.10"),
+        (_NULLABLE_STR, "1984", "1984"),
+        (_NULLABLE_STR, _BODY, _BODY),
+        (_NULLABLE_STR, '"q"', '"q"'),
+        ({"oneOf": [{"type": "string"}, {"type": "null"}]}, "true", "true"),
+        ({"type": ["string", "null"]}, "1984", "1984"),
+        ({"enum": ["1.10", "2.0"]}, "1.10", "1.10"),
+        ({"const": "1.10"}, "1.10", "1.10"),
+        ({"$ref": "#/$defs/S"}, "1984", "1984"),
+        ({"allOf": [{"$ref": "#/$defs/S"}, {"description": "d"}]}, "1.10", "1.10"),
+        ({"$ref": "#/$defs/C"}, "1.10", "1.10"),
+        ({"allOf": [_NULLABLE_STR, {"type": "string"}]}, "null", "null"),
+        ({"$ref": "#/$defs/D0"}, "1.10", "1.10"),
+        (_INT_OR_STR, "1.10", "1.10"),
+        ({"type": ["number", "string"]}, "true", "true"),
+        # ...unless the value decodes to another admitted type
+        (_NULLABLE_STR, "null", None),
+        (_INT_OR_STR, "25", 25),
+        ({"type": ["number", "string"]}, "25", 25),
+        ({"enum": [1, "a"]}, "1", 1),
+        ({"type": ["number", "string"], "enum": [1, "x"]}, "1", 1),
+        ({"anyOf": [{"type": "number"}, {"type": "string"}], "enum": [1, "x"]}, "1", 1),
+        ({"allOf": [{"type": ["number", "string"]}, {"enum": [1, "x"]}]}, "1", 1),
+        # no string admitted, or no type information: decode as before
+        ({"anyOf": [{"type": "number"}, {"type": "null"}]}, "1.10", 1.1),
+        ({"description": "untyped"}, "25", 25),
+        ({"anyOf": [{"type": "string"}, {}]}, "25", 25),
+    ],
+)
+def test_convert_value(schema, raw, expected):
+    params = {
+        "$defs": _DEFS,
+        "properties": {"v": schema},
+        "additionalProperties": schema,
+    }
+    props, extra = parameter_types([{"name": "f", "parameters": params}])["f"]
+    for allowed in props["v"], extra:
+        assert convert_value(raw, allowed, json.loads) == expected

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""JSON types admitted by tool parameter schemas.
+
+XML-style tool parsers receive every argument as raw text. These helpers use
+the parameter's schema to decide whether to keep that text or decode it.
+"""
+
+from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable
+from typing import Any
+
+# Types admitted by each listed parameter of one tool, and by any other
+# parameter (additionalProperties). None means unconstrained.
+ParameterTypes = tuple[dict[str, set[str] | None], set[str] | None]
+
+
+def _json_type(value: Any) -> str:
+    """JSON Schema type name of a decoded JSON value."""
+    if value is None:
+        return "null"
+    if isinstance(value, bool):
+        return "boolean"
+    if isinstance(value, int):
+        return "integer"
+    if isinstance(value, float):
+        return "number"
+    if isinstance(value, list):
+        return "array"
+    if isinstance(value, dict):
+        return "object"
+    return "string"
+
+
+def _schema_types(
+    schema: Any, root: dict, refs: dict[str, set[str] | None]
+) -> set[str] | None:
+    """JSON types a parameter schema admits, or ``None`` if it admits any.
+
+    Covers ``type``, ``const``, ``enum``, local ``$ref``, ``anyOf``/``oneOf``
+    (union) and ``allOf`` (intersection), so that e.g. pydantic's
+    ``Optional[str]`` counts as a string. *refs* memoizes each ``$ref``, which
+    keeps the walk linear and ends cycles.
+    """
+    if not isinstance(schema, dict):
+        return None
+    constraints: list[set[str] | None] = []
+    declared = schema.get("type")
+    if isinstance(declared, str):
+        constraints.append({declared})
+    elif isinstance(declared, list):
+        constraints.append({t for t in declared if isinstance(t, str)})
+    if "const" in schema:
+        constraints.append({_json_type(schema["const"])})
+    if isinstance(schema.get("enum"), list):
+        constraints.append({_json_type(v) for v in schema["enum"]})
+    ref = schema.get("$ref")
+    if isinstance(ref, str):
+        if ref not in refs:
+            refs[ref] = None  # a ref still being resolved is unconstrained
+            node = root if ref.startswith("#/") else None  # e.g. #/$defs/Name
+            for part in ref[2:].split("/"):
+                if isinstance(node, dict):
+                    node = node.get(part.replace("~1", "/").replace("~0", "~"))
+            refs[ref] = _schema_types(node, root, refs)
+        constraints.append(refs[ref])
+    for key in ("anyOf", "oneOf"):
+        if isinstance(schema.get(key), list) and schema[key]:
+            union: set[str] = set()
+            for branch in schema[key]:
+                if (types := _schema_types(branch, root, refs)) is None:
+                    break  # an unconstrained branch admits anything
+                union |= types
+            else:
+                constraints.append(union)
+    if isinstance(schema.get("allOf"), list):
+        constraints.extend(_schema_types(s, root, refs) for s in schema["allOf"])
+    known = [  # an integer is also a number
+        t | {"integer"} if "number" in t else t for t in constraints if t is not None
+    ]
+    return set.intersection(*known) if known else None
+
+
+def parameter_types(tools: Iterable[Any] | None) -> dict[str, ParameterTypes]:
+    """Map tool name to :data:`ParameterTypes`, for Chat or flat Responses tools."""
+    types: dict[str, ParameterTypes] = {}
+    for tool in tools or []:
+        function = getattr(tool, "function", None) or tool
+        if isinstance(function, dict):
+            name, parameters = function.get("name"), function.get("parameters")
+        else:
+            name = getattr(function, "name", None)
+            parameters = getattr(function, "parameters", None)
+        if not name or not isinstance(parameters, dict):
+            continue
+        properties = parameters.get("properties")
+        if not isinstance(properties, dict):
+            properties = {}
+        refs: dict[str, set[str] | None] = {}
+        types[name] = (
+            {k: _schema_types(s, parameters, refs) for k, s in properties.items()},
+            _schema_types(parameters.get("additionalProperties"), parameters, refs),
+        )
+    return types
+
+
+class ParameterTypesCache:
+    """Parameter types of the last tools list seen, built on first use."""
+
+    _last: tuple[Any, dict[str, ParameterTypes]] = (None, {})
+
+    def for_tools(self, tools: Iterable[Any] | None) -> dict[str, ParameterTypes]:
+        if tools is not self._last[0]:
+            self._last = tools, parameter_types(tools)
+        return self._last[1]
+
+
+def convert_value(
+    raw: str, allowed: set[str] | None, decode: Callable[[str], Any]
+) -> Any:
+    """Decode *raw*, but keep the text if the schema admits a string, unless it
+    decodes to another admitted type (``null`` for ``Optional[str]``).
+    """
+    if allowed == {"string"}:
+        return raw
+    decoded = decode(raw)
+    if allowed is None or "string" not in allowed:
+        return decoded
+    return decoded if _json_type(decoded) in allowed - {"string"} else raw

Good catch, that was not intended. I've dropped the change to `extract_types_from_schema`, and `utils.py` is now identical to main.

Routing it through the new walker changed more than your case. `Optional[Model]` (`anyOf: [{"$ref": ...}, {"type": "null"}]`) also lost `null`, so an emitted null came back as the string `"null"`.

So `ParserEngine._coerce_value` and `_coerce_dict`, `_streamable_string_keys`, k2_horizon and minimax_m3 behave exactly as on main. `anyOf: [integer, {}]` gives `["integer", "string"]` again and `5` stays `5`.

The new walk is now used only by the Muse, MiniCPM5 and Poolside parsers. I served `qwen3_coder` on Qwen3.5-0.8B on B200 to check: your `anyOf: [integer, {}]` case returns `5`, and a null for `Optional[Model]` returns `None`, both matching main.

One numeric-type intersection edge at `6647ada2`:

```python
import json
from vllm.tool_parsers.schema_types import ParameterTypes, convert_value

schema = {"type": ["number", "string"], "enum": [1, "x"]}
allowed = ParameterTypes.from_schema({"properties": {"v": schema}}).get("v")
print(allowed)                              # {'string'}
print(repr(convert_value("1", allowed, json.loads)))  # '1'
```

The original Muse helpers decode this as integer `1`, which satisfies the
schema. The new string `"1"` is not in the enum. `jsonschema.Draft202012Validator`
confirms that distinction. Replacing the enum's `1` with `1.0` also makes this
helper decode numerically, although those are the same JSON Schema value.

Could the type-set combination account for `integer` being a subset of
[`number`](https://json-schema.org/understanding-json-schema/reference/numeric#number),
including integral numeric enum values? The `allOf` and `anyOf` equivalents show
the same loss during intersection, before `convert_value`'s numeric adjustment.

Independent CPU component controls: 5 pass / 3 fail. This imports the exact
standalone new module, extracts the unchanged original Muse helper bodies for
comparison, and uses the real JSON Schema validator. It is AI-assisted review,
not a complete parser/HTTP, Rust, model or upstream-suite qualification.

@yzong-rh @bbrowning thanks for raising the shared-utility question. I looked at both overlaps before slimming this PR:

- **Structured outputs** (the xgrammar/guidance feature checks, RFC #58697) asks whether a backend supports the keywords in a whole schema. This PR asks something narrower: does one tool parameter admit a string, so the parser can keep the raw text. The RFC's shared schema layer could host that later.
- **`ParserEngine._coerce_value`**: I tried having the XML parsers call `coerce_to_schema_type(raw, extract_types_from_schema(schema))`. That fixes `Optional[str]` but regresses main elsewhere. Untyped `{}` values get stringified, `"1"` under a boolean schema becomes `true`, `$ref` parameters lose their type, and MiniCPM5/Poolside lose their `literal_eval` fallback. The root cause is that `extract_types_from_schema` returns `["string"]` both for "string" and for "unknown", which is the area #63385 works on.

So the PR now leaves `extract_types_from_schema` and `vllm/tool_parsers/utils.py` identical to main and does not conflict with #63385. The new walk stays private to the Muse, MiniCPM5 and Poolside parsers. On the Rust side, Muse reuses the existing `SchemaRoot::options` walk instead of adding a second one.

Once #63385 lands, I'm happy to do a follow-up that puts these walks and the JSON-type helpers behind one utility.
